response.why: Both Preachers have deathtouch, so a double-block loses both our blockers to their single attacker for a bad 2-for-1; chump blocking with just the Vampire Token preserves our full board (both Preachers) at minimal cost while gaining a point of life, clearly the best value here.
response.plan: Chump block their attacking Preacher of the Schism with the Vampire Token, preserving both of our Preachers and Bat for a dominant board position; continue pressuring with attacks and hold Faerie Mastermind/Kaito for future turns.

response.why: Since none of our remaining spells cost 1 mana, playing the untapped Swamp provides no practical benefit this turn or next (we'd still lack enough mana for Drowner/Mastermind on their turn either way), while playing Undercity Sewers banks a free surveil trigger for no real cost.
response.plan: Play Undercity Sewers for the surveil value; hold the rest of the hand (Mastermind, Drowners, Enduring Curiosity, Bat) for reactive plays once mana is available again on my next turn.

response.plan: Cast Deep-Cavern Bat to see and exile from their 3-card hand, then use the remaining 4 mana on Enduring Curiosity for a big body and card-draw engine; hold Drowners/Mastermind for their turn if any mana remains.

response.why: Passing through combat damage keeps all 6 mana open; the board is already dominant (opponent at 11 life, one blocker up) so there is no urgency to commit Mastermind/Drowner/Enduring Curiosity into open opponent mana during combat. Casting reactively now just telegraphs and risks a 2-for-1 versus holding for the stronger postcombat sequencing (Enduring Curiosity + Bat) or genuine reactive use on their turn.
response.plan: Pass through the remainder of combat damage; in second main phase cast Enduring Curiosity and Deep-Cavern Bat with the 6 available mana, holding both Floodpits Drowners and Faerie Mastermind in hand to use reactively on the opponent's turn. I'd change this only if the opponent's Floodpits Drowner or another response threatens to blow out my open mana before I get to act.

response.why: Deep-Cavern Bat is the standout line: it has no flash so this main phase is our only window to cast it at sorcery speed, it strips a card from the opponent's 3-card hand before their turn (the sims show their hand dropping to 1-2 after), and it only spends 2 of our 6 mana, leaving 4 open to still flash in Floodpits Drowner/Faerie Mastermind reactively. Enduring Curiosity, the Drowners, and Mastermind all have flash, so committing them now in the main phase forfeits ambush value and taps out more mana for no real benefit versus holding them; passing entirely is fine but strictly worse than Bat since it forgoes the hand-disruption this turn while Bat still leaves plenty of mana open. Kaito hardcast is solid development but ties up 4 mana and skips the Bat's info/disruption.
response.plan: Cast Deep-Cavern Bat now to exile the opponent's best card and get a lifelink flyer, holding the 4 remaining mana plus both Floodpits Drowners, Faerie Mastermind, and Enduring Curiosity (all flash) to deploy reactively during their turn - stunning down a big threat like Sheoldred or Kaito if they resolve one. I'd change this only if the exiled-card reveal shows a must-answer bomb that needs an immediate different response.

response.why: Still resolving Deep-Cavern Bat's ETB trigger with nothing threatening us - the logic hasn't changed: holding all 4 mana plus Faerie Mastermind, both Drowners, and Enduring Curiosity keeps maximum reactive flexibility for the opponent's turn, while committing any of them now just taps us down for no benefit since none of these need to be cast at this exact instant.
response.plan: Let the Bat trigger resolve and pass, holding the full 4 mana plus Faerie Mastermind, both Floodpits Drowners, and Enduring Curiosity to deploy reactively on the opponent's turn - stunning a big threat if they land one. I'd change this only if their response demands an immediate answer I can't afford to wait on.

leaves.opp_board: Preacher of the Schism 2/4 T, Vampire Token 1/1, Floodpits Drowner 2/1, Deep-Cavern Bat 1/1, Preacher of the Schism 2/4, Vampire Token 1/1 | 5 lands (0 untapped)

response.why: Double-blocking to send Deep-Cavern Bat into their Enduring Curiosity (chump, absorbing 4) while our Enduring Curiosity blocks their attacking Preacher of the Schism is clearly best: the deathtouch trade kills their Preacher for good (no recursion clause on it), our Enduring Curiosity dies but returns as a permanent enchantment retaining its draw trigger, Bat's lifelink partially offsets the unblocked Floodpits Drowner, and we end at a healthy 16 life. Blocking their Enduring Curiosity with both our creatures also kills a real threat but only converts it to an enchantment on their side too (it has the same recursion clause), so it's less valuable than removing their Preacher outright. Leaving Bat unused (options 4 and 6) wastes a free blocker and costs more life for no extra benefit.
response.plan: Block their Enduring Curiosity with Deep-Cavern Bat and their attacking Preacher of the Schism with our Enduring Curiosity - the deathtouch trade kills their Preacher permanently while ours recurs as an enchantment, taking only their Floodpits Drowner's damage (offset by Bat's lifelink).

response.why: Same reasoning continues: with 6 mana up and nothing forcing our hand at draw step, holding the flash suite (Mastermind, both Drowners) keeps maximum flexibility. Go for the Throat is now in hand too - it's tempting to use on their Preacher of the Schism now, but since it's instant speed there's no cost to waiting for a bigger target (a future Sheoldred or Kaito) or a critical combat moment, so it scores above the other blind commits but still below simply passing.
response.plan: Pass through the draw step, holding the full 6 mana plus Faerie Mastermind, both Floodpits Drowners, and Go for the Throat to develop or react in the main phase and beyond. I'd change this only if a trigger or must-answer play appears.

response.why: Playing our Swamp now is pure upside - it costs nothing from our reactive suite and just banks extra mana for later this turn or the opponent's, so those lines score highest, edging out plain passing. Holding Faerie Mastermind, both Floodpits Drowners, and Go for the Throat still makes more sense than casting them blind before we see what the opponent does; Go for the Throat scores a bit above the creature casts since removal retains proactive value even used reactively, but there's still no reason to commit before a real target or threat appears.
response.plan: Play our Swamp land (free value, no opportunity cost) and pass otherwise, holding the full mana plus Faerie Mastermind, both Floodpits Drowners, and Go for the Throat to develop or react as the turn continues. I'd change this only if a must-answer threat appears.

response.why: Attacking with Preacher of the Schism is clearly correct: since we have more life, the attack trigger guarantees a card draw regardless of block outcome, and the worst case is an even trade (our Preacher for their blocking Preacher, deathtouch both ways) while we still draw a card. In the better sampled outcomes their Vampire Token blocks instead, our Preacher survives, kills the token, and we draw into Kaito. Not attacking is safe but leaves a free card draw and pressure on the table for no real benefit given our commanding life and board lead.
response.plan: Attack with Preacher of the Schism, holding back Enduring Curiosity (now an enchantment, not a body) and keeping the full mana plus Faerie Mastermind, both Floodpits Drowners, and Go for the Throat open to react on their turn. I'd change this only if a surprise trick threatens a bad outcome.

response.why: Still resolving the Preacher attack trigger with nothing forcing our hand. Continuing to hold the flash suite (Faerie Mastermind, both Floodpits Drowners, Go for the Throat) keeps maximum reactive value for the opponent's upcoming turn, regardless of what they do in response to our attack trigger.
response.plan: Pass, letting the attack trigger resolve (draw a card, lose 1 life) and holding the full mana plus Faerie Mastermind, both Floodpits Drowners, and Go for the Throat to react on their turn. I'd change this only if a must-answer threat appears.

response.why: Holding Faerie Mastermind in a 2-card hand (Island being the only other card) risks a future Deep-Cavern Bat exiling it before I ever get to deploy it (leaf 1 is clearly worst). Casting it now removes that exile risk entirely and still lets me hold up its {3}{U} draw-ability as a reactive response to whatever they play, so the 'cast now' leaves cluster higher than the risky 'pass and do nothing' leaf. Kaito hitting the board is the main downside line regardless of my choice since I have no answer for it in hand right now.
response.plan: Lean toward casting Faerie Mastermind proactively to protect it from Deep-Cavern Bat exile and get its draw-trigger online, while still holding remaining mana for the {3}{U} draw ability or future instants; would reconsider only if I drew into removal for Kaito or a reason to hold full mana for a bigger response.

response.why: It's only my draw step with no stack action needed, so passing costs nothing and preserves full flexibility to play my land and choose sequencing in main phase. Committing Faerie Mastermind or Floodpits Drowner right now doesn't add protection or value I couldn't get by waiting until main phase, and Floodpits Drowner in particular is better held for a real flash window (ambushing an attacker or stunning a relevant threat) rather than firing it now on a random already-tapped creature. Go for the Throat killing my Preacher is the worst-case outcome regardless of my choice here since I have no protection for it in hand.
response.plan: Pass through the draw step and move to main phase with full information before deciding whether to deploy Faerie Mastermind (to protect it from a future Deep-Cavern Bat) or hold both flash creatures for reactive value; would only commit early if I saw a reason to bluff or needed the body immediately.

response.why: Since the opponent has more life than us (14 vs 11), attacking with Preacher of the Schism triggers its Vampire-token ability regardless of whether it gets blocked, and its deathtouch/4 toughness means it can't be meaningfully traded down by any of their current untapped blockers. Not attacking forfeits that free value for no safety benefit since Preacher isn't needed as a blocker this turn (Floodpits Drowner and Faerie Mastermind can still block).
response.plan: Attack with Preacher of the Schism (the only eligible, non-summoning-sick attacker) to generate a Vampire token and pressure their life total; hold Floodpits Drowner and Faerie Mastermind back as blockers since they're summoning sick anyway.

response.why: Kaito is a 5/6 attacker our blockers can't kill even in combination (6 toughness vs at most 5 total power), so there's no trade to be had - only damage prevention. Chump-blocking with the Vampire Token is clearly best: it's our least valuable creature, and its lifelink means blocking with it swings our life from 11 (no block) to 12 instead of down to 6, while keeping Floodpits Drowner and Faerie Mastermind alive. Triple-blocking wastes our real creatures for no extra benefit over the token alone.
response.plan: Block Kaito, Bane of Nightmares with the Vampire Token alone - it's expendable, its lifelink still triggers, and it prevents all 5 damage while keeping Floodpits Drowner and Faerie Mastermind as future blockers/threats.

response.why: Using Floodpits Drowner's bounce ability to shuffle away their stunned Preacher of the Schism is strong value since Floodpits Drowner's ETB has already paid off and we're trading an already-spent body for a real, ongoing threat on their side. Sheoldred resolving unanswered remains the worst-case regardless of my line since I have no removal for it in hand. Losing our own Preacher to a follow-up Go for the Throat is a real risk but independent of which line I take.
response.plan: Activate Floodpits Drowner's ability to shuffle their stunned Preacher of the Schism (and Floodpits Drowner itself) into their library, removing a real threat while I still have mana up for Faerie Mastermind's draw ability if something worth responding to comes up.

response.why: Casting the second Preacher of the Schism is the single best action here since it's the only sorcery-speed play available this turn and adds a strong deathtouch blocker/attacker with its own card-advantage triggers - a real board upgrade against their wide, dangerous board with Kaito. Playing a land is close to free value regardless of which one. Floodpits Drowner and the draw ability are better held for reactive flash windows rather than committed now.
response.plan: Cast the second Preacher of the Schism for board presence and a deathtouch blocker, play a land, and hold Floodpits Drowner plus the {3}{U} draw ability for reactive use on their turn or later this turn if needed.

response.plan: Flash in Floodpits Drowner now to get a second blocker before blocks are declared — with only the summoning-sick Vampire Token available otherwise, I'd be forced to take a big hit from Kaito (6) or the deathtouch Preacher (2) unblocked.
response.why: Both of their attackers (Kaito 6/7 and Preacher 2/4 deathtouch) are coming in and I only have one untapped blocker; casting Floodpits Drowner now gives me a second body so I can block both and take zero combat damage instead of dropping to as low as 2 life, which matters even with my huge board/hand lead since a burn spell or another attack next turn could be dangerous.

response.plan: Block Kaito with the Vampire Token (gaining 1 life from its lifelink) and Preacher of the Schism with Floodpits Drowner, taking zero combat damage this turn since neither attacker can be killed by my available blockers anyway.
response.why: With no way to kill either attacker, spreading my two expendable blockers across both attackers prevents all 8 potential damage and even nets a point of life, while every other blocking split leaves at least one attacker unblocked for real damage — not worth risking my life total when I have overwhelming board/hand advantage to close the game with.

response.plan: Play a land this main phase (favoring the tapped duals since I have plenty of mana already) or cast Deep-Cavern Bat for ETB value, while holding Floodpits Drowner and the draw ability in reserve for reactive use rather than tapping out proactively.
response.why: Land drops and Deep-Cavern Bat are the proactive plays with no 'hold' option and are essentially risk-free given my dominant board/hand state, while casting Floodpits Drowner or the draw ability early repeatedly shows me losing a Preacher or Faerie Mastermind to a follow-up removal spell once I'm tapped out — better to develop safely and keep interaction up.

response.plan: Play a land this main phase (favoring a tapped dual since I already have ample mana) or cast Deep-Cavern Bat for ETB value; hold Floodpits Drowner, Faerie Mastermind's cast, and the {3}{U} draw ability in reserve unless combat or an incoming removal spell forces a reactive play. I'd change my mind if I need a surprise blocker before combat or see them tap out into an exposed target worth answering.
response.why: Land drops and Deep-Cavern Bat are proactive, essentially risk-free value with no 'hold' option, while committing extra mana into Floodpits Drowner, Faerie Mastermind, or the draw ability now repeatedly costs me a permanent to follow-up removal once I'm tapped out in sampled branches — better to develop safely and keep mana open for combat tricks/instant-speed value given my commanding 11-vs-5 life and board lead.

response.plan: Cast Floodpits Drowner now in Begin Combat to tap and stun one of their few remaining blockers (a Vampire Token or the summoning-sick Deep-Cavern Bat, since Kaito and their Preacher are already tapped) before I declare attackers, clearing the way for more damage against their 5 life while leaving plenty of mana up for Faerie Mastermind or reactive plays afterward. I'd hold instead only if I saw a must-answer threat resolve that needed my mana for instant-speed removal more urgently than the blocker-denial.
response.why: With the opponent at only 5 life and just a handful of untapped blockers, tapping one down via Floodpits Drowner's ETB directly increases the damage that gets through this combat; it's cheap relative to my 10+ lands so I still keep mana open afterward, whereas passing forgoes this window's tactical value and the {3}{U} draw ability taps me out for no combat-relevant benefit while also handing them a card.

Hold Preacher of the Schism back rather than attacking with it: attacking costs me 1 life from its own trigger with no guaranteed payoff (it can just be chump-blocked by a lifelink Vampire Token, netting them life back), and keeping its deathtouch body up as a blocker is valuable against Kaito, Bane of Nightmares becoming a 3/4 hexproof creature on their turn.
response.why: Faerie Mastermind's evasion makes attacking with it essentially free value (guaranteed damage plus a card, zero risk), which beats both sending everyone (costs me 1 life via Preacher's trigger for a blocked/traded token) and not attacking at all (wastes the turn's damage output while I hold a commanding 11-vs-5 lead). Sending Preacher alone is worst — it can be lifelink-chump-blocked, netting them life while I still pay the self-inflicted life loss from its trigger.

response.plan: Cast Deep-Cavern Bat now — with the opponent down to 3 life and running low on cards, the ETB (look at their hand, exile a nonland card) is high-value disruption, and it adds another evasive lifelink attacker for next turn's kill. I'll still get to play a land drop on a later priority window this main phase; if I only get one action, the land can wait to next turn while Deep-Cavern Bat can't recreate its ETB value later.
response.why: Several sampled lines show the opponent nearly hellbent (down to 1-2 cards) already, so seeing and stripping their hand now is likely to remove their last answer before I go for lethal; it also develops a flying lifelink body that helps close the game. A land drop is safe value but replaceable next turn, whereas Deep-Cavern Bat's one-time ETB is the play that can't be recovered if skipped.

response.plan: Block Kaito, Bane of Nightmares with just Preacher of the Schism — deathtouch guarantees the kill outright while taking zero combat damage, and it's the cheapest way to permanently remove their biggest threat. I'd avoid taking the hit outright (drops me to 4 life, far too risky) and avoid chump-blocking with a non-deathtouch creature (Kaito survives to threaten again) or over-committing multiple blockers (wastes bodies a single deathtoucher already handles).
response.why: Single-blocking with the deathtouch Preacher kills a 7/8 hexproof threat for the cost of one creature and zero life lost, which is strictly better than eating 7 damage (drops me to a dangerously low 4 life), chump-blocking with something that doesn't kill Kaito (leaves it alive to keep attacking), or throwing all four blockers at it (achieves the same kill for a needlessly higher cost when one deathtoucher suffices).

Passing keeps maximum flexibility heading into the attack that ends the game.
